Unfortunately, both now pose significant and ongoing safety, health, maintenance, and insurance concerns, and we believe full removal is the only sustainable solution.1. Safety ConcernsThe Oak (T2) has developed a worsening lean toward the house, particularly over a bedroom. Several large branches have already fallen, raising serious concerns during storms.Its raised roots have also damaged the driveway, creating trip hazards for our children (aged 5 and 8) and elderly parents.2. Security RisksThe large canopies of both trees severely limit visibility of our driveway and front garden. We would also like to install gates, but the uneven driveway caused by roots makes this unfeasible.3. Health & InsuranceThe trees are very close to the house. My 6-year-old son suffers from severe seasonal allergies, and pollen and debris from the trees are contributing.Insurers have also raised concerns about the Oak?s proximity (within 3 meters), limiting our insurance options.4.
